title: The large molecular gas fraction of post-starburst galaxies at z > 1
question: What is the molecular gas content of post-starburst galaxies at z > 1, and what physical mechanisms are responsible for quenching their star formation?

recipe.goal: Extract 1D CO(3-2) spectra, optimize spatial position, and measure line flux and redshift in the uv plane
recipe.method: Iterative uv-plane point-source modelling per channel across all four sidebands, averaging over channels maximizing S/N to fit spatial position, and fitting average line maps in uv plane with a 2D PSF model; Gaussian fit to 1D spectrum allowing for negative continuum for ID97148
assumptions: Targets are spatially unresolved point sources at the angular resolution of the observations

recipe.goal: Measure dust continuum flux densities and upper limits
recipe.method: Integrate spectral range excluding channels dominated by CO emission line, fit 2D PSF model in uv plane at fixed CO position, and stack continuum maps of both targets
key_parameters: 5 sigma upper limit at fixed CO position
assumptions: Point-source profile centered at the CO detection position

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas masses from CO(3-2) luminosity and continuum upper limits
recipe.method: Convert CO(3-2) luminosity to CO(1-0) using excitation ratio r_32 and then to M_H2 using Milky-Way-like alpha_CO; convert continuum upper limits using Rayleigh-Jeans dust emission calibration at 850 um
key_parameters: alpha_CO = 4.4 M_sun K km s^-1 pc^2
beta = 1.8, alpha_850 = 1 x 10^20 erg s^-1 Hz^-1 M_sun^-1
assumptions: Flat LambdaCDM cosmology with Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7, H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; r_32 = 0.5; alpha_CO = 4.4 M_sun K km s^-1 pc^2; optically thin dust continuum with beta = 1.8

recipe.goal: Estimate stellar masses and star formation rates via spectro-photometric SED fitting and [OII] emission
recipe.method: Simultaneously fit multi-wavelength SXDS photometry and VLT/VIMOS optical spectra at fixed spectroscopic redshift using Fast++; also compute dust-corrected [OII] luminosity SFR using Kewley et al. (2004)
key_parameters: log(tau/yr^-1) in [6.5, 10] in log-steps of 0.1; ages in log-steps of 0.1 from 100 Myr to age of Universe; A_V in [0, 6] mag; Z = 0.008, 0.02, 0.05
assumptions: Bruzual & Charlot (2003) models, Chabrier (2003) IMF, delayed SFHs, Calzetti et al. (2000) dust attenuation curve, E(B-V)_star = 0.58 E(B-V)_nebular

recipe.goal: Measure spectral absorption indices and derive stellar population ages
recipe.method: Measure Lick indices H_delta_F, H_gamma_F, and D_n4000 from VIMOS optical spectra and compare with a Monte Carlo library of 500,000 synthetic spectra to construct Bayesian PDFs of R-band light-weighted and mass-weighted mean stellar ages
key_parameters: 10% error added to D_n4000 error budget; median of PDF as fiducial value, 16th and 84th percentiles as uncertainties
assumptions: Zibetti et al. (2017) library of 500,000 synthetic spectra with Sandage (1986) SFHs plus random bursts, varying metal enrichment histories, and 2016 Bruzual & Charlot (2003) / Chevallard & Charlot (2016) SSPs

score_reason: Public ALMA data (2019.1.00900.S), standard pipeline calibration, and well-described uv-plane point-source fitting (with cross-checks between GILDAS uv_fit and CASA uvmodelfit) make the ALMA measurements straightforward to reproduce, though the exact velocity integration windows and optimized extraction coordinates for ID97148 are not explicitly tabulated.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA Band 4 dataset (2019.1.00900.S) is public and small, the uv-plane point-source fitting method is clearly described, and the primary numeric results (CO fluxes, redshifts, line widths, and molecular gas masses for the two targets and two serendipitous companions) are explicitly tabulated.
